content.comment_body: Hello, I am having trouble programming with [product_name] Web Editor. I want to read a temperature transmitter in the web server but cannot access its value online. Additionally, I want to create a set point function to compare the ambient temperature against my set point, but I'm unable to achieve this. Does anyone have a sample on how to control room temperature using a mobile device or web browser? I have attached my program and will send the [product_name] Web Editor file in my next message.

The issue relates to overlapping addresses. For example, bits V0.0 and V0.1 are part of the word VW0. You use V0.1 for manual start in the [product_name] diagram, but in the [product_name] Web Editor project, V1.1 is assigned to this function. As background: 8 consecutive bits form a byte, two bytes make a word, and two words form a double word. For instance, VB0 includes bits V0.0 to V0.7, VB1 covers V1.0 to V1.7, and VW0 comprises VB0 and VB1 (V0.0 to V1.7). VD0 is made up of VW0 and VW2 (VB0 to VB3, V0.0 to V3.7). I could adapt your [product_name] Web Editor project, but I have the current V1.1.0 version. If I do this, you won't be able to open it in older versions.
Thank you very much. How can I download [product_name] Web Editor V1.1.0?

Compatibility: [product_name] Web Editor V1.1 creates custom web pages for earlier hardware, with some new controls available except user-defined web page and PDF. DAMEX check is required for downloads (FAQ, Support ID 109744535).

Hello experts, I have another question. In the attached image, when my AI1 shows 21 Celsius, the web monitor displays 426. I want it to show only 21°C. For the set point, I have to set 300 (VW40); I want this to be 25°C instead. Please advise a solution. AI1: Room temperature, VW40: Set point.
If the attached photo is unclear, please use this [url].
In general, you should already know: a screenshot might be sufficient sometimes, but often it is not. Please upload your [product_name] diagram and Web Editor project.

An AI input in the [product_name] system measures values from 0 to 1000 units. An AI from an analog module also measures 0 to 1000 units, not directly scaled to temperature. You need to scale the AI value using an analog amplifier for physical measurement ranges.
This is my program. Please take a look.
Where is AI1 sourced from—an analog module or an external transmitter? Your [product_name] diagram lacks documentation, so it's not clear. Please provide more information.

Let me rephrase my question. How can I input an analog value in [product_name] Web Editor and compare it with a scaled AI value? My AI is scaled with a gain of 0.05, but my set point range is not accurate. I want to compare a temperature value with a set point.
The temperature transmitter is set to a 0-10V range and measures from 0 to 50°C.
You are using the amplifier within the analog comparator, so both the AI and the set point received from the web server are amplified. This approach enables effective comparison.
Thank you very much, my issue has been resolved.

analysis.insight_summary: The main issue involves displaying real-world temperature readings and managing set points in the [product_name] Web Editor. The user faces confusion over memory addressing, scaling sensor values to physical units, and compatibility between software versions. The user seeks a user-friendly solution for monitoring and controlling room temperature using mobile devices or web browsers, but is challenged by technical details and software limitations regarding raw data, scaling procedures, and bit management.
analysis.user_expectations: The user anticipates an easy configuration and monitoring process for room temperature in actual units (Celsius) through the web interface, with intuitive management of set points and value scaling—ideally requiring minimal specialized programming or technical expertise.
